biography:
Sara has been dedicated to photography and photographic calligraphy since 2006. She inherited the artistic sensibility of her father, a musician and composer, which led her to explore not only the world of theatre — to which she devoted several years both as a performer and as a stage photographer — but also music, studying classical solfège and bass for several years, and cinema, influenced by the Centro Sperimentale di Cinematografia, where her father worked as a sound engineer.

Alongside various courses in photographic techniques and workshops focused on travel reportage, she pursued the training promoted by MoMA on photography as a means of individual artistic expression, as a tool for exploring reality and documenting society, as well as a form of communication and cultural critique. Later, driven by an interest in history, with photojournalism as one of its primary sources, she attended the course on the use of images and films and their historical interpretation in the twentieth century at the University of London & Royal Holloway. In 2022, she joined the platforms “Ninfa. io” and “KnownOrigin.io”, which curate and publish NFT collections, making artworks — and photography NFTs in particular — more accessible to both artists and collectors.

In 2023, she created the book Portraits of NFT Artists, a project dedicated to the dialogue between photography, contemporary art, and new forms of digital expression.

In 2025, she deepened her visual and narrative research through a multidisciplinary path intertwining cinema, photography, and digital experimentation. She attended the course Scandinavian Film and Television at the University of Copenhagen, where she studied the Scandinavian audiovisual system in relation to European and global cultural, institutional, and political contexts, with particular attention to the role of cinema as a vehicle for the social values of Nordic welfare societies. At the same time, she took part in the workshop AI and Creativity – Midjourney, dedicated to the use of artificial intelligence in generative image processes, conducted by Alessandro Bavari. Among her professional activities, she has curated several photographic backstage projects, the latest of which took place at the MACRO Museum in Rome.

After developing a deeper artistic connection with Alessandro Bavari, she further shaped her style through his continuous and daily mentorship. United by photography as an artistic form of expression, as well as by their personal bond, they published together the book Kill the Covid!, a photographic rural horror mockumentary set in the Marche region, faithful to their visionary and provocative artistic language.

In 2026, she created the photographic book Meta-Est, a visual journey through the suspended territories of Eastern Europe and beyond, conveyed through the narrative power of black and white, understood not as an aesthetic choice but as an expressive necessity. An exploration of places where reality transforms into symbol, and where the boundaries between memory, identity, and imagination become blurred.

In the same year, together with Alessandro Bavari, she won first prize for the animated short film Artefatti at the Rome Creative Contest.

Her artistic practice constantly moves between documentation and vision, between traditional languages and emerging tools, offering a poetic and critical perspective on the social and cultural dynamics of Eastern Europe and beyond.
statement:
Her photographic approach, rooted in reportage and street photography, is defined by a strict black-and-white visual language.

Inspired by the cinematic work of Hungarian director Béla Tarr, Sara Aliscioni constructs images shaped by symbolism, drama, and poetry, offering an objective yet deeply emotional interpretation of reality.

Her work often places the human figure at the center of familiar, everyday contexts, where fragility and presence coexist.

A constant thread throughout her research is the pursuit of beauty, even in environments marked by decay, darkness, and oblivion.
